caveats: **Pushes follow a tag set, nothing else.** Deleting a structured tag (REST, dashboard or MCP), an agent that is offline when a tag is set, and an agent reconnecting all send no `sync`, so the local copy can hold a deleted or outdated value until the next structured tag set for that device. Watch `yuzu_server_system_reserved_push_total{result="undelivered"}` for pushes that missed an offline agent.

**`stale` is push recency, not correctness.** It is true when no `sync` landed within `check_interval`, which is the normal state of a device whose tags have not changed, and it is re-evaluated only once per interval. Compare the values themselves with the server when the question is whether the copy is right.

**`sync` replaces the whole copy, and its output is wider than its declared schema.** A hand-dispatched `sync` that omits a category erases it locally and logs a `tag_removed` change. Every real `sync` also emits four `tag|<key>|<value>` rows and a `last_sync|<epoch>` line that the definition's `result.columns` does not describe.

**A stalled data directory stalls every action.** `status`, `get`, `changes` and the staleness thread take the same lock as the file write, so a hung filesystem under `data_dir` blocks all of them, not only `sync`.

**The samples show cold-boot defaults and predate two `status` rows.** The capture harness never calls `init()`, so every sample shows empty tags, `last_sync=0` and `stale=true` rather than any real state file, and `sync` is not captured. All three captures carry `leg-hash pending` and end `status` at `change_count`; the shipped plugin also emits `persist_failures` and `last_persist_error`, so treat the Outputs table, not the sample, as the `status` shape.

definitions.description: Returns the change history for structured asset tags on this device. Each entry records the category key, old value, new value, and timestamp of the change. Useful for compliance auditing and drift detection.
Retrieve a single structured tag value by category key. Valid keys: role, environment, location, service.
Query the agent's locally cached structured tags, last sync time, staleness flag, and change count. No server-side state is modified.

Push the server-assigned structured tags (role, environment, location, service) to an agent. The agent stores them locally and reports any changes from the previous state. Typically invoked automatically by the server when a tag category value changes.

description: Structured asset tag awareness — syncs server-assigned tags locally and detects changes
how_it_works:
`asset_tags` keeps a local copy, on the endpoint, of the four tag categories the server treats as authoritative: `role`, `environment`, `location` and `service`. The server is the only writer. When an operator sets one of those tags through the REST API, the dashboard or MCP `set_tag`, the server reads all four of the device's current values from its TagStore and pushes them to the agent as one `sync` call (a system-reserved push, not an operator instruction). `sync` replaces the whole local copy: the four values are compared with the cache, each difference is appended to a change log (the newest 50 entries are kept), and the new state is written atomically to `<data_dir>/asset_tags.json`. A category that is empty or missing in a `sync` is erased, so a hand-dispatched `sync` that names one category clears the other three locally. `status`, `get` and `changes` only read the local copy. A background thread sets `stale` to true when `check_interval` seconds (default 300, minimum 30) pass without a sync; it never asks for one.

Deliberately not: the tag store that scope targeting uses. `tag:` scope expressions resolve against the server's TagStore and never read this file, and no other agent component reads it. It is also not the free-form tag plugin (`tags`, `content/definitions/tags.yaml`), and it never pulls: the agent never initiates a sync.

outputs_note: Every action writes one or more pipe-delimited lines via `ctx.write_output`. There is no single row shape shared across an action's own output: `get` emits exactly one `tag|<key>|<value>` line per call, and `changes` emits one `change|<key>|<old_value>|<new_value>|<timestamp>` line per recorded change followed by `total_changes|<n>` (or the sentinel line `changes|none` when the log is empty, with no trailing count on that path). `status` and `sync` each emit several different line shapes in one response: `sync` writes `sync|no_changes` or one `sync|<event>|<key>|...` line per change, then four `tag|<key>|<value>` lines and `last_sync|<epoch>`. There is no shared empty-result placeholder convention: an unset tag reports as an empty string, never `-`. Every string field on every row — values, keys, and the echoed text of the two error rows (`unknown action: …`, `error|unknown category: …`) — is escaped with the shared `safe_output_field` (`|` becomes `\|`, CR/LF become a space, a literal backslash is folded to `/`), so a value such as `Rack A|3` renders as `Rack A\|3` in a stable row shape. The stored value is never rejected or stripped; the backslash fold is a limitation of the shared server decoder and applies on the wire only. Values are capped at 448 bytes on `sync` and again on load from disk.

result_status.when: `sync`: the new state was written to `<data_dir>/asset_tags.json` with no warning, or no data dir is configured and there is nothing to write

`sync`: the temp-file write or the rename over `asset_tags.json` failed (data dir not creatable, not a directory, disk error, or on Windows another process holding the file open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`); the reason is in the agent log

`sync`: the file was written but re-asserting owner-only mode (`fchmod` to 0600) failed; the file is never wider than 0600 (created at `0600 & ~umask`) but may be narrower, so the next load may fail; outranks `persist_dir_unsynced` when both occur (the status row's `last_persist_error` carries both causes)
`sync`: the file was written and renamed but the parent-directory fsync failed, so the rename is durable only after the next OS flush

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only** for row data. Rows reach the ResponseStore through the standard command-response path, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Trigger and delivery metric.** `sync` is sent by the server, never directly by an operator: a structured tag-category set through the dashboard `tag.set` handler, REST `PUT /api/v1/tags` or MCP `set_tag` calls the same `push_asset_tags_to_agent` closure. Each push increments `yuzu_server_system_reserved_push_total{capability="asset_tags.sync"}` with `result` `sent` or `undelivered` (the agent was not connected); this is a delivery metric, not row data.
**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX or metrics. No other agent component reads `asset_tags.json`.

**Sensitivity.** `role`, `environment`, `location` and `service` are free-form organizational tags an operator assigns, and can reveal a device's physical site or business role. Values are byte-capped (448 bytes) but not content-validated: an operator can type anything into them, including a hostname, a serial or a person's name, so classify by what is actually assigned, not by the category name. The on-disk copy is owner-only (`0600`) on POSIX.
**Siblings:** `tags` (`content/definitions/tags.yaml`) is the general-purpose, agent-authoritative free-form key/value store; `asset_tags` holds only the four server-authoritative categories.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) then `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) then `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("device.asset_tags.status")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
